PhD & MFA: Application & Deadlines
Graduate Information
We welcome your PhD or MFA application to Boston University’s Graduate School of Arts and Sciences (GRS)!
Arts & Sciences is Boston University’s largest academic division, the heart of a world-class research university. Our faculty in the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS) are among the world’s most respected professors, researchers, and professionals in their disciplines. Our alumni are leading innovation and research and making an impact in their fields. Our campus is Boston, a city vibrant with history, culture, and diversity, and teeming with potential for connections and careers.
Boston University offers many similar sounding programs (ex: Biology, Neurobiology, Oral Biology, and Biomedical Engineering are each offered by a different graduate school). If you are applying to a program that is not offered by Graduate School of Arts and Sciences (GRS), for example Bioinformatics or Neuroscience, please reach out to the respective schools directly, for example:
⇒ College of Engineering (ENG): Biomedical Engineering, Computer Engineering, etc.
⇒ Faculty of Computing & Data Sciences (CDS): Bioinformatics
⇒ Graduate Medical Sciences (GMS): Biomedical Sciences, Neuroscience, Neurobiology, etc.
⇒ Wheelock College of Education (SED): Counseling Psychology, Social Studies in Education
⇒ Other schools/programs
Important Admissions Update
Our fall 2027 PhD & MFA applications are now open (except for the programs noted below). If you have any questions about a GRS program (required application materials, writing samples, test scores, class sizes, research opportunities, career outcomes, decision timelines, etc.) that are not already answered below (or in our Admissions FAQs), please contact the program directly and not the graduate school’s central admissions office. The program contact information can be found below.
Does GRS offer my PhD or MFA program?
There are over 40 institutions of higher education in the Boston area, many with similar sounding names. Boston University alone has 17 separate graduate schools (ex: Communication, Engineering, Fine Arts, Medical Sciences, …, and Arts and Sciences). For example, Bioinformatics degrees are offered by Boston University’s Faculty of Computing & Data Sciences (CDS), and Neuroscience degrees are offered by Boston University’s Graduate Medical Sciences (GMS).
We only serve students of & applicants to Boston University’s Graduate School of Arts and Sciences (GRS). Please do not contact our office if we do not offer your program and do not ask us to provide you with contact information for other Boston University schools or other Universities in the Boston area. If you have questions about a Boston University program that is not offered by GRS, please reach out to the respective office directly:

Admissions Basics
Applications and all supporting documents must be submitted to the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS) through our online application.
You must use your full legal name as it appears on official government documents (passport, birth certificate, or social security card, etc.) when filling out university applications, documents, and corresponding with the our office. To ensure compliance with legal documentation and handle a high volume of inquiries and files, we must use legal names exclusively.
We strongly advise that you familiarize yourself with our PhD & MFA: Frequently Asked Questions before contacting our admissions staff.
Applications close at 11:59pm (23:59) Boston Time (Eastern Time Zone, UTC – 05:00) on the day listed as the program’s application deadline (refer to the list of programs at the bottom of this page). Example: if the deadline is listed as December 15, then the application will close on December 15 at 11:59pm Boston time. If you are currently located in a time zone west of Boston (i.e. UTC – 06:00 to UTC – 11:00), you must submit your application one to six hours before midnight your time. Please do not wait until the very last second to submit your application. We do not grant extensions. Please plan ahead.
You cannot apply to more than one GRS program, and you cannot apply to both a GRS PhD and a GRS Master’s degree. We recommend that you contact the program directly if you are unsure about applying to the Master’s or the PhD degree. PhD & MFA applicants can only apply to the fall semester.
You can apply to a program offered by GRS and program(s) offered by the other sixteen Boston University schools and colleges.
When creating your account, please be sure to use a permanent, non-school or employer-issued email address. You will be contacted through the email address you use to create the account, and correspondence may occur after your previous school disabled your school or work email account. Having a “prestigious” email address does not boost your chances for admission.
Letters of recommendation are received separately. You don’t need to wait for them to submit your application. Your recommenders will submit their letters separately.
All documents (transcripts, personal statement, CV/resume, writing sample, if applicable, etc.) have to be submitted through the online application before the application deadline. Documents that are sent or emailed directly to the Graduate School of Arts and Sciences by you, your institution, or a third party (ex: Parchment) cannot be added to your application. You cannot add or email updated documents (personal statement, resume/CV, etc.) or transcripts (showing fall grades for example) after you submit your application.
We cannot add updated transcripts (showing fall grades for example) to your application after submission/after the deadline.
All documents, official electronic test scores, and recommendations letters must be received by the deadline; otherwise, they may not be considered by the program’s application review committee. Please allow for 5-10 business days for electronic scores (GRE, TOEFL, IELTS, etc.) to be matched to your application.
All credentials, including transcripts and recommendation letters, submitted in support of an application become property of Boston University. Neither originals nor copies may be returned.
After you submit your application, it will be reviewed by the program’s admission committee (not the Graduate School’s central admissions office). The response time varies by program. Most programs make admission decisions in late February to early March. If you have questions about the timeline, please contact the program directly. Once a decision has been made, you will receive an email informing you of the outcome.
If you are a PhD or MFA applicant to the Graduate School of Arts and Sciences (GRS) and have a program-related question, please contact the program directly at the email address listed under each program (refer to the list of programs at the bottom of this page).

Statement on Holistic Admissions
The admissions committee of each of our graduate programs will be looking, as always, at the entire transcript and the cumulative GPA in their evaluation as well as test scores (if applicable), recommendations, and personal statements, as required by specific programs. We encourage applicants to include special circumstances as well as achievements that may not be apparent due to modified grading policies in their personal statements.
As part of our holistic approach to admissions, many of our PhD programs no longer require the GRE General Test, while others have suspended the requirement for applicants. For those who continue to use it, they do so as part of their holistic review. While GRE scores may be an essential component of the application for some programs, they are only one of many factors that contribute to your review as an applicant. Our programs consider the personal statement, letters of recommendation, GPA, and other supporting materials, when assessing an applicant’s academic potential and ability. Please refer to the Application Requirements listed under each program to see which program does/does not require the GRE.

Playwriting (MFA)
Boston University’s MFA program in Playwriting program is no longer accepting applications and will conclude once current students have completed their degrees. Students interested in writing for the stage or screen may wish to explore other opportunities at Boston University, including the MFA in Screenwriting in the College of Communication. The Boston Playwrights’ Theatre is now part of Boston University’s Office of the Arts, which advances artistic expression and creative engagement across the University through its programs, partnerships, and venues. The theater, along with the Office of the Arts’ other artistic spaces and initiatives, continues to support artists, present new work, and contribute to the university’s cultural and educational life. We are proud of the Playwriting program’s long history and the many writers it has helped develop and wish prospective playwrights the best in their future endeavors.
